PROBABILITY_YES: 45
REASON: A slim majority of economists in the latest Reuters poll (19 of 34) now expect a 25bp hike, after Macklem's hawkish 17 October remarks, firm surveys showing rising expectations, and oil well above the Bank's July assumption, alongside Fed and ECB hikes. Against that, core measures are below 2%, employment has fallen two months running and new US tariffs weigh on growth. That gives a meaningful case for waiting, so the decision is close to a coin flip with a slight lean toward a hike.

PROBABILITY_YES: 45
REASON: A slim majority of economists (19 of 34 in the Reuters poll) now expect a 25 bp hike, after Macklem signalled on 17 October a higher inflation forecast and a greater risk that inflation broadens, and the Fed and ECB have both hiked. Against that, core inflation is below 2%, headline CPI came in under expectations, employment fell in both August and September, and new US tariffs weigh on growth. That leaves the decision close to a coin flip, leaning slightly toward a hike.

PROBABILITY_YES: 45
REASON: A narrow majority of economists in the 21-23 October Reuters poll (19 of 34) expect a 25 bp hike. That follows Macklem's hawkish 17 October signals, rising inflation expectations in the Bank's own surveys, oil back above US$110, and hikes by the Fed and ECB. On the other side, core inflation is below 2%, employment has fallen two months running, and new US tariffs are hitting growth, so a hold is still quite possible; I put the decision close to a coin flip, leaning slightly towards a hike.

PROBABILITY_YES: 47
REASON: Most economists in the latest Reuters poll (19 of 34) now expect a hike, and Macklem's hawkish signals point toward tightening: higher inflation forecasts, rising expectations in Bank surveys, oil above US$110, and the Fed and ECB already hiking. Against that, core inflation is below 2%, employment fell sharply in August and September, tariffs are cutting growth, and the September CPI came in soft, so holding remains a strong possibility. That leaves the decision close to a coin flip, with a slight lean toward a hike.
